summary: No rentals exist. The broker collects marketplace offers, weighs boot time and pull cost against price, provisions the best one, and records the release disposition: today's full decide-and-provision path. The machine is fresh and it is still not the Run's to destroy. This listing sells reusable capacity, so what the placement takes is a lease, and cleanup takes Mercator's workload off the host and leaves the lease standing. A listing selling a one-shot execution instead would record a terminate here, which is the only kind of capacity a Run's own ending takes with it. Neither candidate is a machine that exists, so neither records a Rental Schedule: evidence for capacity with no Rental behind it would publish a queue read off a schedule that does not exist.
